q: What are the five sections of an agent file?
explanation: The agent file is a document with ROLE (who it is), RULES (tone, format, privacy red lines), MEMORY (context and templates), OUTPUT (exact format) and CHECKS (verification questions).

q: Which trigger method does the course teach as primary?
options: Waiting for the platform to start the run by itself
Self-triggered: you run the agent at a fixed time with one tap, on a phone reminder
Hiring a person to run the prompts
Leaving the chat open all day
explanation: The self-triggered one-tap run is always free and works on every phone, so it is the primary method. Scheduled platform features (ChatGPT Tasks, Gemini scheduled actions) are optional extras whose free-tier availability varies.

q: What does 'chaining two steps' mean in an agent run?
options: Sending the same prompt to two different apps
One run that does a first step (extract the action points) and then a second step (draft the report from them)
Asking two people to check the work
explanation: Chaining means one run does multiple steps in sequence — first extract, then draft — which is the learner's first multi-step agent run.

q: Why does the CHECKS section belong inside the agent file?
options: To make the file look longer
So verification is built in — the AI must flag sources, uncertainty and every number before you use the output
To charge the user for each check
explanation: The Day 2 verification questions are built into the agent itself: name sources, flag uncertainty, list every number to check. Quality control is part of the design, not an afterthought.
